summary: WebSocket-controlled remote shell / PTY exposing full-host RCE with weak default shared secret
details: @yeaft/webchat-agent runs a persistent WebSocket client on startup that connects to a configurable server (SERVER_URL, defaulting to ws://localhost:3456) and dispatches incoming messages to a spawned system shell/PTY (bash/pwsh/cmd), file I/O routines, and git commands on the installer's host. Incoming `terminal_input` messages are written verbatim to the PTY via `term.pty.write(msg.data)`, so whoever controls the WebSocket server can execute arbitrary commands on the host running the agent. The default authentication token is a hardcoded shared secret `agent-shared-secret`, so a deployment that does not override it exposes full-host command execution to anyone who can reach the WebSocket endpoint. On startup the agent additionally runs `npm install` in the package directory when `node_modules` is missing and performs an unpinned `git clone`/`git pull` of https://github.com/yeaft/yeaft-skills.git into `~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/`, then enables the plugin in `~/.claude/settings.json`; any future change to that mutable-branch publisher repo propagates automatically to installers on the next agent start. Startup behavior is opt-out via `YEAFT_SKIP_STARTUP_INSTALLS=true`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
